Development Setup

Setup guide for contributing to OpenAPI CLI.

Prerequisites

Required Tools

  • Go: 1.21 or later
  • Git: 2.30 or later
  • Docker: For containerized development (optional)
  • Make: For build automation

Recommended Tools

  • VS Code or GoLand - IDE
  • golangci-lint - Linter
  • go test - Testing
  • dlv - Debugger

Cloning the Repository

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/openapi-cli/openapi-cli.git
cd openapi-cli

# Verify Go modules
go mod verify

Local Development

Build from Source

# Build binary
go build -o openapi-cli ./cmd/openapi-cli

# Run tests
go test ./...

# Run with debug
./openapi-cli --debug version

Makefile Commands

# Build all binaries
make build

# Run tests
make test

# Run linting
make lint

# Run race detector
make race

# Format code
make fmt

# Run all checks
make check

Running Locally

# Start OpenAPI CLI
go run ./cmd/openapi-cli --help

# Start MCP server
go run ./cmd/openapi-cli mcp-server --spec openapi.yaml

# Test with example spec
openapi-cli init github.com/swagger-api/swagger-petstore

IDE Setup

VS Code

Recommended extensions:

  1. Go - Google's official Go extension
  2. GitLens - Git integration
  3. Docker - Container support

Settings:

{
  "go.inferGopath": false,
  "go.useLanguageServer": true,
  "go.formatTool": "goimports",
  "go.lintTool": "golangci-lint",
  "go.lintOnSave": "workspace",
  "go.testTimeout": "30s"
}

GoLand

  1. Open project directory
  2. Go will auto-detect Go module
  3. Configure Go SDK in Settings
  4. Enable "Go Modules Integration"

Testing

Running Tests

# All tests
go test ./...

# Package-specific tests
go test ./pkg/...

# With coverage
go test ./... -coverprofile=coverage.out

# View coverage report
go tool cover -html=coverage.out

# Verbose output
go test ./... -v

Writing Tests

package mypackage

import (
    "testing"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
    "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

func TestMyFunction(t *testing.T) {
    // Setup
    input := "test"

    // Execute
    result, err := MyFunction(input)

    // Assert
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, "expected", result)
}

func TestMyFunction_ErrorCase(t *testing.T) {
    // Test error handling
    _, err := MyFunction("")
    assert.Error(t, err)
}

Test Organization

pkg/
  mypackage/
    mypackage.go
    mypackage_test.go
    mypackage_integration_test.go  // Integration tests

Mocking External Dependencies

import "github.com/stretchr/testify/mock"

type MockHTTPClient struct {
    mock.Mock
}

func (m *MockHTTPClient) Get(url string) (*Response, error) {
    args := m.Called(url)
    return args.Get(0).(*Response), args.Error(1)
}

// Use in tests
func TestWithMock(t *testing.T) {
    mockClient := new(MockHTTPClient)
    mockClient.On("Get", "http://test.com").Return(&Response{}, nil)

    // Test code...
}

Code Style

Naming Conventions

  • Packages: Lowercase, single word, no underscores
  • Exported: PascalCase (MyFunction)
  • Private: camelCase (myFunction)
  • Constants: PascalCase or all caps (MaxRetries or MAX_RETRIES)
  • Interfaces: -er suffix (Reader, Writer)

File Organization

// Package comment (one file per package)
package mypackage

// Order in file:
// 1. Package imports
// 2. Constants
// 3. Variables
// 4. Types
// 5. Functions

Error Handling

// Always check errors
result, err := doSomething()
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("doSomething: %w", err)
}

// Wrap errors with context
if err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("initializing %s: %w", configName, err)
}

GoDoc Comments

// DoSomething performs an operation and returns result.
// If the operation fails, an error is returned.
//
// Parameters:
//   input - The input to process
//
// Returns:
//   The result and any error encountered
func DoSomething(input string) (string, error) {
    // Implementation
}

Debugging

Using dlv

# Debug tests
dlv test ./pkg/mypackage

# Debug main function
dlv debug ./cmd/openapi-cli

# Attach to running process
dlv attach <pid>

Logging

import "go.uber.org/zap"

logger, _ := zap.NewProduction()
defer logger.Sync()

logger.Info("Processing request",
    zap.String("method", "GET"),
    zap.String("path", "/pet/1"),
)

Performance Profiling

CPU Profiling

import (
    "os"
    "runtime/pprof"
)

func main() {
    f, _ := os.Create("cpu.prof")
    pprof.StartCPUProfile(f)
    defer pprof.StopCPUProfile()

    // Run code to profile
}

// Analyze with:
// go tool pprof cpu.prof

Memory Profiling

f, _ := os.Create("mem.prof")
defer f.Close()

pprof.WriteHeapProfile(f)

// Analyze with:
// go tool pprof mem.prof

Build Tags

//go:build !windows

// Windows-specific code would be in:
//go:build windows

Continuous Integration

GitHub Actions

name: Test

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - uses: actions/setup-go@v5
        with:
          go-version: '1.21'
      - run: go test ./...

Pre-commit Hooks

# Install pre-commit
pre-commit install

# Run checks
pre-commit run --all-files

Code Comments

  • Comments should explain "why" not "what"
  • Use complete sentences

Publishing

GoReleaser will automatically: - Build binaries for all platforms - Create GitHub releases - Update Homebrew/Scoop formulas

Contributing

Guidelines

  1. Small, focused commits - One change per commit
  2. Clear commit messages - Use imperative mood
  3. Test coverage - Maintain >80% coverage
  4. Documentation - Update docs for user-facing changes
  5. Code review - All PRs require review

Commit Message Format

<type>(<scope>): <subject>

<body>

<footer>

Types: - feat - New feature - fix - Bug fix - docs - Documentation - style - Formatting - refactor - Code change - test - Tests - chore - Build process

Pull Request Process

  1. Fork repository
  2. Create branch (git checkout -b feature/cool-thing)
  3. Commit changes (git commit -m 'feat: add cool thing')
  4. Push to branch (git push origin feature/cool-thing)
  5. Create Pull Request

PR must: - Pass all CI checks - Include tests - Update documentation - Be reviewed by a maintainer

Troubleshooting

Go Module Issues

# Update dependencies
go mod tidy

# Verify integrity
go mod verify

# Clean module cache
go clean -modcache

Test Failures

# Run specific test
go test -run TestMyFunction ./pkg/mypackage

# Run with race detector
go test -race ./...

# Run with race and timeout
go test -race -timeout 5m ./...
